Emily — thanks for the clear notes and the workbook, that helps a lot. Quick answers up front:

- Minimum-commitment ramp: we can add a 30-day grace for the first quarter (one-time), but trailing usage will be reconciled against the commitment at quarter end.
- Net terms: Net45 is possible but requires finance sign-off and a small billing admin fee (0.5% of quarterly invoice) for accounts that push beyond Net30 — I'll get an explicit number from billing.

Looping in Kimberly for legal redline guidance on how to accept the midpoint change with minimal MSA edits. Karthik — heads up that Evergreen wants Net45; can you own the finance approval?

Camila / Emily,

Thanks — quick legal read below and a suggested language snippet for the Order Form/Appendix A. High level: midpoint pricing for tranches is commercially acceptable provided the Order Form makes explicit how rounding and proration work for partial-tranche usage. We should avoid touching the MSA; keep the change localized to the Order Form appendix to preserve downstream compatibility.

Suggested language (to include in Appendix A, new paragraph after Pricing table):
"For purposes of tranche pricing, the applicable per-unit rate for any month shall be determined by the midpoint rate of the tranche that corresponds to the Customer's usage for that month. Partial-tranche usage shall be prorated on a pro rata basis by token-hour or equivalent metric and rounded to the nearest cent. The onboarding tranche (Month 0–1) shall remain billed at the top-of-band rate to cover onboarding and burst capacity.
"
On Net45: we can accept Net45 as an exception. To keep the MSA intact, we'll put the billing admin fee as a commercial note in the Order Form (not in MSA) and include a clause: "Net45 applies subject to completion of Redwood's standard credit checks; a billing-administration fee of 0.5% of each quarterly invoice will apply." If Evergreen's legal requires the fee to be 0.0%, we should escalate to revenue ops.

I will redline EVG_OrderForm_v3 and return with tracked changes; Camila, please advise if you'd like me to remove proposed template boilerplate or keep it visible for the customer's lawyers.

—Kimberly
